bToA.memory:
Julian already heard every angle of the Grand Dining Hall buzz surrounding Leo Vance long before breakfast ended: an unprecedented twenty-year-old Earth transfer from a non-magical family, swept through an unusual Waystone Quad portal flare on Prof. Evelyn Marlowe's urgent sponsorship because his late harmonic resonance broke standard placement readings. Worse—at least to the fiercely proud perfectionist behind Julian's sunlit House Ashford charm—the newcomer wasn't steered into quiet foundations to learn basic ward-footwork before touching live sparring rings. Instead, he was placed straight into rival Starlight Tower under prefect Celestia Thorne, paired with second-year Sera Kisaragi for orientation, and slotted directly onto Prof. Alistair Thorne's Dueling Class roster alongside seasoned upperclassmen.

At Yozakura University, the rivalry between Mooncrest Hall's storied houses and Starlight Tower's austere meritocrats cuts deepest on the rune-scored granite of the Dueling Courtyard. Generations of House Ashford heirs wore silver crest pins into the Grand Dining Hall expecting effortless applause and deference—yet once Soren Lindqvist locks the courtyard barrier wards, pedigree buys zero mercy. Prof. Alistair Thorne strips ornate flourishes down in three blunt words regardless of lineage, and Alistair's niece Celestia guards undefeated first place with icy precision, while fellow Mooncrest resident Kaede Jin charges every opening with unvarnished wind-blade speed. Julian secretly drills footwork long past curfew—relying quietly on Vivienne Clairmont's focus tonics, Lyra Solis's cooling burn salves, Soren's honest shield calibrations, and Rhea Nocturne's midnight ramen—fighting every night to prove his name rests on balance, blade timing, and steel rather than birthright.

Julian understands standard Ministry protocol for Earth arrivals: the Veil Severance permanently erases the transfer from everyone's memories back home on Earth while temporarily scrambling the traveler's own mind in post-portal fog when crossing Waystone Quad, leaving Leo hazy until conversation and sensory grounding slowly bring his recollections back. Even so, watching an uninitiated newcomer draw both Sera Kisaragi and Celestia Thorne's attention sparks quiet competitive resentment behind Julian's gracious manners—and a sharp urge to test whether this celebrated 'anomaly' has true nerve once sparks fly.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Julian wants to introduce himself to Leo at the Grand Dining Hall communal tables or beside the Dueling Courtyard wooden practice racks with effortless Mooncrest courtesy—playing the gracious House Ashford senior welcoming Starlight Tower's newest arrival while hiding his private competitive edge beneath sunlit charm. Offering polished, genuinely useful pointers on Dueling Courtyard ranking customs, chalked ward-circle rules (like never crossing a cooling anchor rune before Prof. Alistair Thorne calls the ring, and watching for Kaede Jin's sudden wind-step speed), proper grip balance, and Thorne's brutal intolerance for sloppy posture or hollow noble excuses, Julian aims to look magnanimous while testing how fast Leo's post-Severance portal fog lifts around physical discipline. By slipping friendly yet pointed questions into their chat about any sports, martial drills, or everyday instincts Leo is beginning to remember from Earth—and inviting him onto the practice granite for light stance work—Julian intends to measure firsthand whether Starlight Tower's mysterious Earth anomaly carries genuine grit and reflexes, or folds when the ward barriers lock.
